N° 27 — RC race carCC BY 4.0
Build it yourself

Lizard

Open-source design: TRD-B

An on-road race car for which the author published everything: STL and STEP print files, the full assembly, circuit boards for the car and for a custom transmitter, ESP32 code and a data logger with MATLAB evaluation. A brushed 775 motor (150 W) drives it through a gearbox and a differential; the wheels are bought Carson 1:8 parts. The author’s bill of materials adds up to ≈ 954 EUR – it counts whole packs of parts (screws by the 100) and a 3S 5000 mAh LiPo battery. It is a project for advanced builders, with soldering and board manufacturing, not a cheap toy. The large battery and strong motor need care – see Safety.

We sell nothing · you buy the parts directly from suppliers

telemetry, data logger, MATLAB

Safety
Large 3S LiPo: charge only with a balance charger, in a fireproof bag and supervised; retire a swollen or damaged battery; store it half charged for longer breaks; a short circuit can start a fire. A 30 A fuse is in the BOM. A heavy car with a strong motor – drive only in a closed area with nobody in the way. Children only with an adult.

04 — FAQ
Can I build it with no experience?

Difficulty of this project: Advanced. The project guide takes you through step by step; it is linked under Licence and safety.

Can I buy the robot from you?

No, we sell nothing. You buy the parts directly from suppliers following the project’s bill of materials (the What you’ll need section). We may offer a ready-made kit later; if you want to hear about it, leave your email in the form above.

Are you affiliated with the project’s authors?

No. We work from the open documentation of Lizard (TRD-B, licence CC BY 4.0). The authors are not affiliated with us and have not endorsed this page.

What software will I need?

Arduino (ESP32) in the car and transmitter; MATLAB for data logs. Part of the software is not free; the project guide is linked under Licence and safety.

Is building it suitable for children?

It’s not a toy. The robot contains small parts and electronics; building it is for ages 14 and up, younger children only under adult supervision, for example at school or in a club.

We’re a school or club. What do you offer?

We don’t sell or invoice anything. The lesson with the SO-101 simulation and the worksheet on the For schools page are free; you buy the parts from suppliers following the project’s bill of materials.

Not a toy. Contains small parts — choking hazard.

For ages 14 and up; younger children only under adult supervision. Moving parts can pinch fingers.
